commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5 (#25009)

Bumps LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream
(llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
(ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
`Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
upstream corrected it:
- Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
- The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: setup_metadata

commit_message:
[HAL] Reject buffer view size overflows (#24992)

Rejects dense buffer views when shape multiplication or packed byte-size
calculation exceeds `iree_device_size_t`. Previously, overflowing
dimensions could wrap to a small value and produce an undersized
allocation request.

The size calculation now uses checked multiplication and addition while
preserving zero-dimension behavior and sub-byte element packing. Dense
view creation also verifies that the logical byte length fits within the
backing buffer, and reshape validates element counts before updating
metadata.

Tests cover:

- Shape products that wrap to zero or one.
- Packed-byte multiplication and addition overflow.
- Maximum-size byte and sub-byte element counts.
- Zero dimensions following otherwise overflowing dimensions.
- Dense views larger than their backing buffers.
- Overflowing reshape attempts.
- Native and forced 32-bit `iree_device_size_t` configurations.

Tested with:

- `iree/hal/buffer_view_util_test`
- `iree/hal/string_util_test`
- `iree/tooling/buffer_view_matchers_test`
- `iree/tooling/function_io_test`
- `iree/tooling/numpy_io_test`
- Repository pre-commit hooks for all changed files

The original `iree-run-module` reproducer was not rerun because the
validation build was configured as runtime-only without compiler tools.

This addresses the concrete buffer-view overflow case tracked in #3844.
The broader size-arithmetic audit remains open.

AI agents assisted with understanding the codebase, writing tests, and
reviewing the solution.

---------

Signed-off-by: goutamadwant <workwithgoutam@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

calculation exceeds `iree_device_size_t`. Previously, overflowing
dimensions could wrap to a small value and produce an undersized
allocation request.

The size calculation now uses checked multiplication and addition while
preserving zero-dimension behavior and sub-byte element packing. Dense
view creation also verifies that the logical byte length fits within the
backing buffer, and reshape validates element counts before updating
metadata.

Tests cover:

- Shape products that wrap to zero or one.
- Packed-byte multiplication and addition overflow.
- Maximum-size byte and sub-byte element counts.
- Zero dimensions following otherwise overflowing dimensions.
- Dense views larger than their backing buffers.
- Overflowing reshape attempts.
- Native and forced 32-bit `iree_device_size_t` configurations.

Tested with:

- `iree/hal/buffer_view_util_test`

validation build was configured as runtime-only without compiler tools.

- Dense views larger than their backing buffers.
- Overflowing reshape attempts.
- Native and forced 32-bit `iree_device_size_t` configurations.

Tested with:

- `iree/hal/buffer_view_util_test`
- `iree/hal/string_util_test`
- `iree/tooling/buffer_view_matchers_test`
- `iree/tooling/function_io_test`
- `iree/tooling/numpy_io_test`

The original `iree-run-module` reproducer was not rerun because the
validation build was configured as runtime-only without compiler tools.

This addresses the concrete buffer-view overflow case tracked in #3844.
The broader size-arithmetic audit remains open.

reviewing the solution.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result
unpack, but not both.

The unpack is the last op of its group, so a consumer of a claimed
unpack gets its own dispatch instead of fusing with the unpack. An
unpack that its root does not claim becomes a root at its own position,
as without the options. Other fusion decisions are unchanged.

No pipeline enables the options yet. A follow-up enables them for
modules whose layouts are materialized before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5 (#25009)

Bumps LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream
(llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
(ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
`Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
upstream corrected it:
- Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
- The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Runtime][Bindings] support async parameter file loading (#24988)

Add support to the parameter providers for asynchronous I/O
so HAL drivers can stream archive data without retaining a host mapping.

And preserve the existing mmap contract for callers that rely on host
allocations while making descriptor-backed loading an explicit opt-in.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Bound static workgroup counts by target limits

A single workgroup-mapped scf.forall with a static count above the
target's max_workgroup_count hit the `continue` in the static-count
branch of resolveWorkgroupForAll and skipped the affine.min bound, so
the exported workgroup count could exceed the target limit. Oversized
counts now fall through to the bound, and the generated loop still
covers the full iteration range. Counts at or below the limit are
unchanged.

Adds a regression test covering counts above, at, and below the limit.

Fixes #24999

Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows (#24987)

Add `--dispatch_statistics` to report a per-function breakdown of
dispatch time beneath each `iree-benchmark-module` benchmark. Rows
include calls per model iteration and each function's share of total
dispatch time, across participating devices and benchmark repetitions.
They appear in console, JSON, and CSV output, including
`--benchmark_out` files and the Python wrapper's results.

After each measured repetition, Google Benchmark reruns the registered
benchmark outside the measured interval with a HAL statistics session on
every device. Profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting,
and asynchronous concurrency as measurement. These extra invocations can
advance model state. Output processing retains the measured pass's
outputs, including snapshots of buffers that subsequent invocations can
overwrite.

Conflicting device profiling, capture, and replay flags are rejected
before sessions start or replay output is opened. The tooling profiling
session API accepts explicit options, and benchmark-module device
profiling covers all participating devices.

Example with the included dispatch-statistics fixture:

```sh
iree-compile \
  --iree-hal-target-device=local \
  --iree-hal-local-target-device-backends=llvm-cpu \
  tools/test/iree-benchmark-module-dispatch-statistics.mlir \
  -o /tmp/dispatch-statistics.vmfb

iree-benchmark-module \
  --module=/tmp/dispatch-statistics.vmfb \
  --device=local-task --task_topology_group_count=2 \
  --function=main \
  --input=64x64xf32=1 --input=64x64xf32=1 --input=64x32xf32=1 \
  --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --time_unit=us --dispatch_statistics
```


Example output from a macOS arm64 run with two `local-task` workers
(timings vary):

```text
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benchmark                                            Time             CPU   Iterations UserCounters...
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BM_main/process_time/real_time                    23.1 us         35.3 us         6181 items_per_second=43.226k/s
BM_main/main_dispatch_0_matmul_64x64x64_f32       8.17 us         12.1 us         6181 calls=2 percent=82.6871
BM_main/main_dispatch_2_matmul_64x32x64_f32       1.71 us         3.21 us         6181 calls=1 percent=17.3129
```

The 64×64 dispatch runs twice per model iteration, so its `Time`
includes both calls. `percent` is the share of total dispatch time; the
first row reports end-to-end model latency. On this CPU backend, the
dispatch rows' `CPU` column sums worker time across dispatch tiles.

Assisted by AI.

---------

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows (#24987)

Add `--dispatch_statistics` to report a per-function breakdown of
dispatch time beneath each `iree-benchmark-module` benchmark. Rows
include calls per model iteration and each function's share of total
dispatch time, across participating devices and benchmark repetitions.
They appear in console, JSON, and CSV output, including
`--benchmark_out` files and the Python wrapper's results.

After each measured repetition, Google Benchmark reruns the registered
benchmark outside the measured interval with a HAL statistics session on
every device. Profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting,
and asynchronous concurrency as measurement. These extra invocations can
advance model state. Output processing retains the measured pass's
outputs, including snapshots of buffers that subsequent invocations can
overwrite.

Conflicting device profiling, capture, and replay flags are rejected
before sessions start or replay output is opened. The tooling profiling
session API accepts explicit options, and benchmark-module device
profiling covers all participating devices.

Example with the included dispatch-statistics fixture:

```sh
iree-compile \
  --iree-hal-target-device=local \
  --iree-hal-local-target-device-backends=llvm-cpu \
  tools/test/iree-benchmark-module-dispatch-statistics.mlir \
  -o /tmp/dispatch-statistics.vmfb

iree-benchmark-module \
  --module=/tmp/dispatch-statistics.vmfb \
  --device=local-task --task_topology_group_count=2 \
  --function=main \
  --input=64x64xf32=1 --input=64x64xf32=1 --input=64x32xf32=1 \
  --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --time_unit=us --dispatch_statistics
```


Example output from a macOS arm64 run with two `local-task` workers
(timings vary):

```text
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benchmark                                            Time             CPU   Iterations UserCounters...
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BM_main/process_time/real_time                    23.1 us         35.3 us         6181 items_per_second=43.226k/s
BM_main/main_dispatch_0_matmul_64x64x64_f32       8.17 us         12.1 us         6181 calls=2 percent=82.6871
BM_main/main_dispatch_2_matmul_64x32x64_f32       1.71 us         3.21 us         6181 calls=1 percent=17.3129
```

The 64×64 dispatch runs twice per model iteration, so its `Time`
includes both calls. `percent` is the share of total dispatch time; the
first row reports end-to-end model latency. On this CPU backend, the
dispatch rows' `CPU` column sums worker time across dispatch tiles.

[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows (#24987)

Add `--dispatch_statistics` to report a per-function breakdown of
dispatch time beneath each `iree-benchmark-module` benchmark. Rows
include calls per model iteration and each function's share of total
dispatch time, across participating devices and benchmark repetitions.
They appear in console, JSON, and CSV output, including
`--benchmark_out` files and the Python wrapper's results.

After each measured repetition, Google Benchmark reruns the registered
benchmark outside the measured interval with a HAL statistics session on
every device. Profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting,
and asynchronous concurrency as measurement. These extra invocations can
advance model state. Output processing retains the measured pass's
outputs, including snapshots of buffers that subsequent invocations can
overwrite.

Conflicting device profiling, capture, and replay flags are rejected
before sessions start or replay output is opened. The tooling profiling
session API accepts explicit options, and benchmark-module device
profiling covers all participating devices.

Example with the included dispatch-statistics fixture:

```sh
iree-compile \
  --iree-hal-target-device=local \
  --iree-hal-local-target-device-backends=llvm-cpu \
  tools/test/iree-benchmark-module-dispatch-statistics.mlir \
  -o /tmp/dispatch-statistics.vmfb

iree-benchmark-module \
  --module=/tmp/dispatch-statistics.vmfb \
  --device=local-task --task_topology_group_count=2 \
  --function=main \
  --input=64x64xf32=1 --input=64x64xf32=1 --input=64x32xf32=1 \
  --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --time_unit=us --dispatch_statistics
```


Example output from a macOS arm64 run with two `local-task` workers
(timings vary):

```text
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benchmark                                            Time             CPU   Iterations UserCounters...
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BM_main/process_time/real_time                    23.1 us         35.3 us         6181 items_per_second=43.226k/s
BM_main/main_dispatch_0_matmul_64x64x64_f32       8.17 us         12.1 us         6181 calls=2 percent=82.6871
BM_main/main_dispatch_2_matmul_64x32x64_f32       1.71 us         3.21 us         6181 calls=1 percent=17.3129
```

The 64×64 dispatch runs twice per model iteration, so its `Time`
includes both calls. `percent` is the share of total dispatch time; the
first row reports end-to-end model latency. On this CPU backend, the
dispatch rows' `CPU` column sums worker time across dispatch tiles.

Assisted by AI.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5 (#25009)

Bumps LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream
(llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
(ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
`Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
upstream corrected it:
- Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
- The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: linux-x86_64 :: Build py-compiler-pkg Package

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5 (#25009)

Bumps LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@7e751154a0e5. The GPU min/maxnumf carry
patch is dropped now that it landed upstream
(llvm/llvm-project@2e686411fa67).

Compatibility changes:

- Migrate AMDGPU target handling from the deprecated `amdgpu::Chipset`
(ISA version numbers) to `ROCDL::TargetInfo` (target feature queries),
following llvm/llvm-project@155462f440ff. The upstream AMDGPU/ROCDL
lowering entry points now take a `ROCDL::TargetInfo`, and the remaining
`Chipset` uses in IREE are migrated too since the deprecation warnings
fail the Bazel `-Werror` build. Behavior is preserved except where
upstream corrected it:
- Barriers on targets without hardware barrier back-off (e.g. gfx90c)
use the inline-asm `s_barrier` form, matching upstream.
  - OCP fp8 conversions are also recognized on gfx11.7.
- The wave64 flag for the HIP platform globals is derived from the
target, so wave32-only targets such as gfx1250 are handled correctly.
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced by
llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[HAL] Reject buffer view size overflows (#24992)

Rejects dense buffer views when shape multiplication or packed byte-size
calculation exceeds `iree_device_size_t`. Previously, overflowing
